rubrics.justification: The response explicitly states no image was provided and relies almost entirely on the Gardner 3AB label rather than analyzing visible morphology. It also inaccurately paraphrases TE grade B as 'few cells forming a loose epithelium,' which is closer to a poorer TE description than standard B-grade criteria.

It integrates most relevant factors well, including age, BMI, PCOS, prior live birth/miscarriage/ectopic, sperm parameters, and endometrial thickness, and relates them to prognosis, though some interactions are somewhat generalized.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with conclusions generally supported by the presented factors. Minor issues include an arguably optimistic implantation estimate and some overinterpretation of endometrial thickness and prior live birth as strong predictors.

Most recommendations are broadly guideline-consistent, including SET and lifestyle optimization, but there are notable deviations: overstatement of 3AB as 'excellent,' routine suggestion of PGT-A in a 31-year-old based mainly on one miscarriage, and mention of immunologic testing/OHSS monitoring without strong case-specific indication.

Provides clear practical steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, lifestyle changes, luteal support continuation, and contingency planning. It is useful, though some recommendations are generic and a few are not tightly tailored to this exact case.
